episodes.label: Shoulders of Giants — Ion Channels & Gene Editing: NaV1.6 (SCN8A), Parvalbumin Interneuron Failure & Adenine Base Editing Rescue of Epilepsy
episodes.notes: Five-Act biophysical and genetic capstone tracing voltage-gated sodium channels from Hodgkin & Huxley (1952), Catterall's DIII-DIV IFM fast-inactivation latch, Raman & Bean's resurgent Na+ current (1997), Miriam Meisler's cloning of Scn8a (NaV1.6) and discovery of human SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (2012), and Gaudelli & David Liu's invention of CRISPR Adenine Base Editors (2017) to recent brain-slice electrophysiology proving how gain-of-function SCN8A drives parvalbumin interneurons into premature depolarization block and synaptic failure (Miralles, Patel et al. 2024 JCI Insight, PMC11529981) and in vivo AAV adenine base editing rewriting R1872W back to wild-type to rescue seizures and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (Reever, Meisler, Farber, Patel et al. 2026 JCI, PMC12871382).

episodes.label: Shoulders of Giants — Neuropharmacology & Bioenergetics: Nicotinic Allostery, SARM1/NAMPT & Rescuing Axons After Blast TBI & Metabolic Stress
episodes.notes: Five-Act historical and biophysical exploration of two intertwined neuropharmacological frontiers: (1) selective alpha-7 and alpha-4-beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor allostery and desensitization in prefrontal cognitive dysfunction (from Loewi, Changeux & Freedman to Cincotta, Yorek MS et al. 2008 and modern PAM/muscarinic therapeutics), and (2) the Wallerian degeneration WldS/SARM1/NAMPT NAD+ survival switch—showing how subclinical pattern-ERG diagnostics after blast-mediated traumatic brain injury identify a therapeutic window where the NAMPT activator P7C3-S243 prevents chronic visual loss (Dutca, Pieper, Harper et al. 2014, PMC5102342) alongside NRK1/2 nicotinamide riboside salvage (Trammell, Brenner et al. 2016, PMC4882590).

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 109: Axelrod's COMT Discovery, Nitrocatechol Tolcapone Mg2+ Coordination, Levodopa Wearing-Off Extension vs. Delayed Hepatotoxicity & Mitochondrial Uncoupling. A person with Parkinson’s disease gets part of his afternoon back. Ten weeks after adding tolcapone, he opens the same diary to write down when his urine darkened. The Critical Care Clinician reads the motor diary, then follows aminotransferases, bilirubin and INR. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs COMT discovery, magnesium coordination and the evidence for a possible mitochondrial liability. The patient, test values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook anchor is the 2010 chapter *Biochemistry and Pharmacology of Catechol-O-Methyltransferase Inhibitors*, which reviews the recombinant human inhibition result. At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes.
